title: Rust FragmentSender does not revalidate revocable policy after construction
description: Rust FragmentSender validates a FragmentationPermit only in new(), then stores only remote signer identity. start/get_fragment/timeout/handle_ack never revalidate the permit, Link key generation, or authenticated peer Rule version. After accept_peer installs an incompatible policy or Link unpins/rotates the key, an existing sender keeps emitting fragments. Retain exact revocable Link/policy evidence and validate on every state-producing transition, invalidating atomically on retirement. Add stale-after-construction tests for version mismatch, unpin, rekey, timeout, and ACK paths.
notes:
Final correctness review: raw public start(), get_fragment()/iter(), timeout(), handle_ack(), write_next() still operate without current policy/link/authority revalidation, so an existing sender can continue after permit retirement by choosing the raw method instead of *_current/*_with_authority. Seal raw transitions as private/test-only mechanics or make current evidence mandatory in the public type API.
Independent Rust security review confirmed every raw public sender transition remains reachable and bypasses the newly added *_current/*_with_authority paths; treat this as P1 production-auth bypass, not compatibility-only polish.
